To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the doublelysine ERlocalisation motif of OST48 is not sufficient to cause ER retention, but is required for ERlocalisation when complexed with ribophorins.
the doublelysine ERlocalisation signal of OST48 is not essential to retain this protein in the ER and that the doublelysines in OST48 are probably involved in complex formation with riboprorin I.
the doublelysine retention motif of OST48 is not sufficient to retain OST48 on its own in the ER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural signals that determine the localisation of pig OST48 to the endoplasmatic reticulum

the structural requirements for ERlocalisation of pig OST48 and indicates that OST48 localises to the ER by virtue of its luminal domain and not by the doublelysine ERlocalisation signal in the cytosol.
the identification of structural signals which are involved in ERlocalisation of pig OST48.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERlocalisation of pig OST48 is a consequence of the presence of its large luminal domain and its complex formation with riboprorin I.

ERlocalisation of pig OST48 is conferred by the luminal domain of this protein, which interacts with a luminal domain of ribophorinin I, and the Cterminal doublelysine motif of OST48 acts as a relocation motif rather than a retention signal.
the doublelysine signal of OST48 is a cytosolic relocation signal which operates in conjunction with ribophorins to retain OST48 within the ER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERlocalisation of pig OST48 is mediated by the ribophorin 1 interaction.
OST48 contains no ERlocalisation signal in its luminal domain but is targeted to the ER by complex formation with other proteins.

ERlocalisation of the pig OST48 protein is achieved by the combined effects of a doublelysine motif within the cytosolic tail and the presence of a ribophorin 1 binding site within its luminal domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the luminal domain of OST48, in addition to the transmembrane domain, is involved in ERlocalisation of this protein.
ERlocalisation of the pig OST48 subunit is conferred by a combination of signals, the most important one being a luminal domain interaction with ribophorins.

OST48 is a typical type I transmembrane protein and that the luminal domain of OST48 interacts with the luminal domain and the transmembrane domain with the transmembrane domains of the ribophorin family.
